rules.rule:
BeeKeeping tests. Check that:
- Each acceptance rule the change claims has a test, and the test would fail if the rule broke.
- Tests build data with the demo company factories. No real names, keys, bank numbers or customer data.
- Ledger tests check balances through reports or the ledger tables, never by trusting a document's own total.
- Tests that touch several organizations assert that one organization can't read or change another's rows.
- No test depends on the current date without fixing the clock.

BeeKeeping tests. Check that:
- Each acceptance rule the change claims has a test, and the test would fail if the rule broke.
- Tests build data with the demo company factories. No real names, keys, bank numbers or customer data.
- Ledger tests check balances through reports or the ledger tables, never by trusting a document's own total.
- Tests that touch several organizations assert that one organization can't read or change another's rows.
- No test depends on the current date without fixing the clock.

BeeKeeping services hold reusable mechanics, per the code-structure skill. Check that:
- The code never imports the database client, Drizzle tables or the session, and never reads or writes BeeKeeping's tables. Code that does belongs in an action.
- Every input arrives as a parameter, and every expected failure returns { ok: false, reason } instead of throwing.
- Money is bigint minor units through the money service. No floating-point math on amounts. Rounding is half up, line by line.
- Calls to Stripe, Plaid, Resend, Claude or storage never log keys, tokens, bank numbers or whole request bodies.
- A new service has at least two callers, or docs/execution-plan.md lists it as a service. Otherwise the code belongs in its action.

BeeKeeping actions decide who may do something, whether it is allowed now, what it means in the ledger and what the user sees. Check that:
- Each action checks the caller's role and takes the organization from the action context, never from input.
- Postings go through the shared postEntry action only. Nothing inserts into journal tables directly, and posted entries are never updated or deleted; a correction is a reversing entry.
- System accounts such as receivables and payables are found by role, never by account number.
- Each write action is registered with its kind (read, draft, post or admin) and its approval category, and supports dry_run and an idempotency key.
- Money is bigint minor units. Exchange rates and tax rates keep their documented precision.
- Failures return a reason code and a plain message. No stack traces or secrets reach the caller.

BeeKeeping schema and migrations. Check that:
- Every new table that holds organization data has org_id, a row-level security policy on org_id, and composite foreign keys that keep references inside one organization.
- Money columns are bigint minor units, and rate columns are numeric with the documented precision.
- Ledger tables keep their guarantees: a line is a debit or a credit, never both and never negative; entries balance at commit; posted rows can't be updated or deleted.
- Audit triggers cover new tables with an explicit list of fields, and secret columns stay off that list.
- A migration that changes or drops existing data says so in a comment at the top, with a tested way back or the reason there is none.

BeeKeeping's MCP server is generated from the action registry. Check that:
- Every tool maps to a registered action and keeps that action's role, scope and approval category. No tool skips approvals or offers admin actions.
- Read tools carry the read-only annotation. Write tools take dry_run and an idempotency key.
- Results never include secrets or unmasked bank numbers, and free text that came from documents is marked as untrusted data.
- Lists page with a cursor and stop at 100 rows. Report tools require a date range.
- Sign-in follows the MCP authorization spec. Tokens are bound to BeeKeeping as their audience and never passed on to other services.

BeeKeeping's web app is a thin layer over actions. Check that:
- Server actions and route handlers only parse input with zod, build the action context from the session and call one action. Business rules found here belong in packages/actions.
- No secret, key or bank number reaches a client component, a log or an error page.
- Pages meet WCAG 2.1 AA: labelled controls, keyboard access, visible focus and enough contrast in both themes.
- Amounts are formatted through the money service, never with floating-point math.

BeeKeeping's worker runs jobs and agent routines. Check that:
- Jobs call actions, carry an idempotency key, report success or failure per item, and never stop a whole run because one item failed.
- Agent routines run under their own agent identity, use only the tools their routine allows, respect run limits and approval policies, and log every tool call to the run record.
- Text from documents is treated as data. Nothing in a memo, a vendor name or an email body can change what a routine is allowed to do.

Shell scripts. Check that the script starts with set -euo pipefail, quotes every variable, and fails when a check it runs fails. A SlowBooks startup check piped its output into tail and could never fail.
GitHub Actions workflows. Check that actions are pinned to a release or commit, permissions are the least the job needs, secrets never reach logs, and every check step fails the job when it fails.

Other BeeKeeping TypeScript. Check that money is bigint minor units, nothing logs a secret, `any` appears only with a comment saying why, and shared logic sits in services or actions as the code-structure skill describes.
